correctness.rationale: Under a uniform initial interval point, conditional shell-position distributions remain uniform through contractions, ordinary doublings and the top-shell reset. Hence the exact dyadic-shell chain moves +/-1 away from zero, and at a doubling from depth zero draws a geometric G with Pr(G>=d)=2^-d. Coupling to the same-sign Skorokhod-reflected simple random walk makes M-W nonnegative, nonincreasing except at a zero-reset, yielding Pr(max_{k<=N}(M-W)>=d)<=Np2^-d. For each fixed p>1/2 the chain has negative drift off zero and positive recurrent visits to 0 at linear rate; independent geometric extremes attain log_2 N almost surely (Borel–Cantelli on dyadic times). Under p_N=1/2+beta/sqrt(N), the sign triangular array has drift -2beta/sqrt(N) and variance tending to 1, so Donsker plus continuous Skorokhod reflection and o_P(sqrt N) path error prove J1 convergence. Brownian level sets have zero Lebesgue occupation, supporting the deep-shell occupation functional limit. Integrating 2 Phi-bar(a/sqrt t) over t in [0,1] yields the stated 2(1+a^2)Phi-bar(a)-2a phi(a). Independent numerical quadrature checked the expectation formula for a=.1,.4,1,2 to machine precision. Reviewed actual rational-coordinate checker.py. The log optimality assertion only holds at fixed p>1/2, not uniformly in the window.

value.rationale: A uniform error coupling of an actual random interval trajectory to a standard reflected walk gives quantitative pathwise control through the intermittent transition, identifies the optimal order of approximation, and transfers a whole-path functional limit and a nontrivial deep-shell occupation statistic. This is a motivated mechanism-level refinement beyond first moments or stationarity and applies at all finite horizons via a usable tail bound.
